title: TotallyLegal Scraper: UK Legal Jobs
description: Scrape UK legal job listings from TotallyLegal.com: title, employer, location, salary, posting age and, on request, the full text, practice area, PQE, contract, hours and workplace. Pay-per-result.
readme:
# TotallyLegal Jobs Scraper Scrape job listings from TotallyLegal ([totallylegal.com](https://www.totallylegal.com/)), the UK job board for lawyers, paralegals and legal support staff. You get the title, employer, location, salary text with parsed amounts when the advertiser states a period, the age of the listing, the closing countdown and the New and Featured badges for every job. Turn on the job page option to add the full description, the exact posting and closing time, the employer page, practice areas, PQE levels, job titles, contract, hours and workplace. Search by keyword, location, job title, practice area, job type and workplace, or start from a TotallyLegal jobs address. ## What you get - One row per job, with parsed salary numbers (from and up to, in GBP) when the salary text names a period such as per annum, per hour or per day. - Optional job page details: exact posting and closing time, full description as HTML and plain text, employer page, reference, recruiter type, practice areas, PQE levels, contract types, hours, workplaces and salary bands. These columns are filled only with the job page option on (detail-only columns). - Each job once per run, even when several keywords find it. - A run with an input that has none of the fields below returns 5 jobs for the keyword paralegal. ## Use with AI Agents (MCP) Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client: Claude Desktop, Claude.ai, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or custom agents. **Apify MCP server URL:** `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=santamaria-automations/totallylegal-jobs-scraper` **Example prompt once connected:** > "Use `totallylegal-jobs-scraper` to find up to 5 jobs for the keyword "paralegal" (paralegal jobs in the UK). Return results as a table with title, company, location and job URL." Clients that support dynamic tool discovery (Claude.ai, VS Code) receive the full input schema automatically. ## Input Every field is optional. Example: ```json { "includeDetails": false, "maxResults": 5, "maxResultsPerQuery": 5, "searchQueries": [ "paralegal" ] } ``` | Field | What it does | |---|---| | `searchQueries` | Keywords such as paralegal, employment solicitor, conveyancer or legal secretary. Each keyword is its own search. Leave empty to read the newest jobs. | | `startUrls` | TotallyLegal list addresses: `https://www.totallylegal.com/jobs/` or a `https://www.totallylegal.com/jobs//` address (slugs combine, for example `/jobs/manchester/paralegal/`), with an optional `?Keywords=...`. A `/searchjobs/` address with only Keywords is read as `/jobs/?Keywords=...`; any other `/searchjobs/` address is skipped, because the site's robots.txt disallows `/searchjobs/` and `sort=`. Page numbers are ignored; reading starts at page 1. Paths that robots.txt disallows (`/jobs/permanent/`, `/jobs/contract/`, `/jobs/full-time/`, `/jobs/recruitment-agency/`, `/jobs/recruitment-consultant/`, `/jobs/direct-employer/`, salary band paths) are rejected with a message in the run status. Use the filter fields instead. | | `locations` | Places the site lists: london-greater-, south-east-england, north-west-england, south-west-england, west-midlands-region, east-of-england, yorkshire-and-the-humber, manchester, west-midlands, europe. London and Greater London work too. Other place names are tried as typed. Each value is its own search. | | `jobTitles` | Only jobs with these job title groups: paralegal, in-house-counsel, solicitor, lawyer, associate, legal-secretary, conveyancer, legal-finance, marketing-business-development, partner. Spaces and capitals are fine (Legal Secretary). Each value is its own search. | | `practiceAreas` | Only jobs in these legal specialisms: child-law, commercial-litigation, commercial-property, employment, family-matrimonial, litigation, private-client, residential-property-conveyancing, trusts-investments-funds, wills-and-probate. Other specialisms are tried as typed (for example aviation). Each value is its own search. | | `jobTypes` | Temporary or part-time jobs: temporary, part-time. Full-time, permanent and contract are not offered because the site's robots.txt disallows those paths. | | `workplaces` | Only jobs with this workplace: hybrid, on-site, remote. | | `maxResultsPerQuery` | Jobs per keyword or start URL. Default 50, up to 1000. | | `maxResults` | Jobs in total. 0 means no limit. | | `includeDetails` | Read each job page for the extra fields. Default false. Same price. | Every list address is a `/jobs/` path of the site, for example `https://www.totallylegal.com/jobs/manchester/?Keywords=paralegal`, with the page number as a path segment from page 2 on. The filter fields are the `/jobs//` segments of the site. The site shows only its top links per filter, so the fields take free text and turn it into a slug (lower case, spaces and `&` to `-`); a slug the site does not know gives no jobs. There is no sort option, no salary band, PQE, employer type or full-time, permanent and contract filter: the site's robots.txt disallows those paths and `sort=`, so the actor never requests them. A value for one of those is skipped with a warning in the log. A filter that is given with only such values ends the run with 0 jobs. Each keyword runs as its own search, combined with each chosen value of each filter (one value per filter in each search, at most 60 searches per run). A job found by several searches is returned once. ## Sample output ```json { "id": "4060316", "title": "Employment Solicitor", "slug": "employment-solicitor", "company": "Motus Recruitment", "company_id": "d1347c59-ca8b-45d0-93d6-a9b685396340", "company_url": "https://www.totallylegal.com/employer/d1347c59-ca8b-45d0-93d6-a9b685396340/motus-recruitment", "company_logo": "https://www.totallylegal.com/getasset/a0fae6cd-2bbc-43ef-b062-6fe5aaee88c1/;w=148", "location": "Hampshire", "region": "Berkshire", "country_code": "GB", "location_terms": [ "South East England", "England", "United Kingdom", "Europe", "Berkshire", "South East England", "England", "United Kingdom", "Europe", "Surrey", "South East England", "England", "United Kingdom", "Europe", "Hampshire" ], "salary_text": "£55k - 65k per year + Outstanding bonus scheme", "salary_min": 55000, "salary_max": 65000, "salary_period": "year", "salary_currency": "GBP", "salary_bands": [ "£50,000 - £59,999", "£60,000 - £69,999" ], "description_short": "Employment Solicitor or AssociateThames Valley/HampshireTop-Tier Employment Team | Leading-Ranked Partners£Highly competitiveJoin a Legal 500 Top Ti", "description_html": "

Employment Solicitor or Associate

Thames Valley/Hampshire

Top-Tier Employment Team | Leading-Ranked Partners

//. It is the dedup key. | | `title` | string | Job title as shown on the listing. | | `slug` | string, null | Text part of the job address. | | `company` | string, null | Employer or recruiter name as shown on the listing. | | `company_id` | string, null | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Id of the employer page (the uuid in /employer//). | | `company_url` | string, null | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Employer profile page on TotallyLegal. | | `company_logo` | string, null | Logo image URL of the employer. | | `location` | string, null | Location text as shown on the listing. | | `region` | string, null | Detail mode only (includeDetails). County or region of the first place in the job posting data. A job with several places lists them all in location_terms. | | `country_code` | string, null | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Country code from the job posting data. | | `location_terms` | array | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Location hierarchy terms of the job, from the specific county up to the continent. Empty when the page has none. | | `salary_text` | string, null | Salary as typed by the advertiser, for example 'Negotiable' or '£55k - 65k per year + bonus'. | | `salary_min` | number, null | Lower bound in GBP, read only from a text with a stated period (per annum, hour, day, week, month). Null otherwise. | | `salary_max` | number, null | Upper bound in GBP, read only from a text with a stated period. 'Up to X' gives only the maximum. Null otherwise. | | `salary_period` | string, null | year, hour, day, week or month; set together with the amounts. | | `salary_currency` | string, null | GBP when the amounts were read, else null. | | `salary_bands` | array | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Salary band terms the site files the job under (for example '£50,000 - £59,999'). Empty when none. | | `description_short` | string, null | Teaser text of the listing card. | | `description_html` | string, null | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Full job description as HTML. | | `description_text` | string, null | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Full job description as plain text. | | `posted_text` | string, null | Age text of the listing card, for example '15 days ago'. Not every card shows it. | | `posted_date_estimated` | string, null | Date worked out from posted_text and the run date (day precision). Exact value: date_posted in detail mode. | | `closing_text` | string, null | Closing text of the listing card: '6 days left' or 'Expiring today'. Not every card shows it. | | `closing_date_estimated` | string, null | Date worked out from closing_text and the run date (day precision). Exact value: valid_through in detail mode. | | `date_posted` | string, null | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Exact posting time from the job posting data, ISO 8601. | | `valid_through` | string, null | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Closing time from the job posting data, ISO 8601. | | `is_new` | boolean | True when the card carries the green 'New' badge (added in the last 2 days). | | `is_featured` | boolean | True when the card is a premium (featured) listing. | | `reference` | string, null | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Advertiser reference. | | `external_job_id` | string, null | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Id of the job in the advertiser's system, as given in the page data. | | `recruiter_id` | string, null | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Internal id of the recruiter or employer account, as given in the page data. | | `recruiter_type` | string, null | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Recruitment Agency or Direct Employer. | | `application_method` | string, null | Detail mode only (includeDetails). How applications are taken, for example Email. | | `listing_type` | string, null | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Listing product of the job, for example 'Job Posting Standard 28 Days'. | | `direct_apply` | boolean, null | Detail mode only (includeDetails). directApply flag of the job posting data. | | `employment_types` | array | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Employment types from the job posting data (TEMPORARY, FULL_TIME, ...). Empty when none. | | `practice_areas` | array | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Legal specialisms of the job. Empty when none. | | `pqe_levels` | array | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Years of post qualification experience asked for. Empty when none. | | `contract_types` | array | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Contract type labels (Permanent, Contract, Temporary, Graduate / Internship). Empty when none. | | `hours` | array | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Hours labels (Full Time, Part Time). Empty when none. | | `job_titles` | array | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Job title groups of the site that the job is filed under. Empty when none. | | `workplaces` | array | Detail mode only (includeDetails). Workplace labels (Remote, Hybrid, On Site). Empty when none. | | `job_url` | string | Job page on TotallyLegal. | | `details_fetched` | boolean | True when the job page was read for this row. | | `search_query` | string | The search that found the job: the keyword with its filter slugs in brackets, the start URL, or 'all jobs'. | | `source` | string | Source host. | | `scraped_at` | string | Time the row was built, ISO 8601 (UTC). | ## Pricing This Actor uses pay per event. There is a small `apify-actor-start` event when a run starts and one `job-result` event for each job in the dataset. You are never charged for a job twice, and a run stops when it reaches the maximum charge you set. Price: $0.001 start fee per run, then $0.0015 per job result ($1.50 per 1,000 jobs). **New to Apify?** Every account gets a $5 free monthly platform credit, enough to try this actor at no cost. ## Related Actors - [Reed.co.uk Jobs Scraper: UK Jobs & Salaries](https://apify.com/santamaria-automations/reed-uk-scraper): UK jobs and salaries from Reed. - [Totaljobs Scraper: UK Jobs, Salaries & Descriptions](https://apify.com/santamaria-automations/totaljobs-scraper): UK jobs, salaries and descriptions from Totaljobs. - [JobServe UK Scraper: IT Contract, Engineering, Finance Jobs](https://apify.com/santamaria-automations/jobserve-uk-scraper): UK IT contract, engineering and finance jobs from JobServe. - [Michael Page Scraper](https://apify.com/santamaria-automations/michaelpage-scraper): Professional jobs from Michael Page. ## FAQ **How many jobs can one search return?** A search or the job list shows 30 jobs per page. The actor reads page after page until the site's "Found N jobs" count is reached, the last page is reached, or your limit is reached. The site lists about two thousand jobs in total. **Is the posting date exact?** With `includeDetails` on, yes: `date_posted` and `valid_through` come from the job page. With it off, the list shows only an age such as "15 days ago" and a countdown such as "6 days left". `posted_date_estimated` and `closing_date_estimated` are worked out from them and the run date, so they can be off by a day. **Why is the salary parsed for only some jobs?** Advertisers type the salary freely. Texts such as "Competitive" or "Circa £500pd" are returned as `salary_text` only. The numbers `salary_min`, `salary_max`, `salary_period` and `salary_currency` are filled when the text states an amount range and a period (per annum, per hour, per day, per week or per month). **What happens when a keyword finds nothing?** The site answers such a search with an HTTP 404 page that has its normal layout and "Found 0 jobs". That is an empty result, not a block. The run ends normally with the status "0 jobs found for ." and nothing is charged for jobs. **What if the site blocks a page?** The site's firewall sometimes answers with an "Error 403" page. The actor retries the page a few times and then once more by another route. If a job page still cannot be read, the row is delivered with its list fields only and the run status says how many job pages were missed. If list pages cannot be read at all, the run ends with a clear "Blocked" status. ## Support Something broken, or a field you wish this Actor returned? Open a ticket on the Actor's [Issues tab](https://apify.com/santamaria-automations/totallylegal-jobs-scraper/issues) or email contact@nanoscrape.com. We usually respond within one working day.
